13479.html:
13479 suptá 'asleep' VS., 'lain down to sleep' R. [√svap¹]
    Pa. sutta- 'asleep', n. 'sleep'; Dhp. sutu 'asleep'; Pk. sutta- 'asleep, lying down'; Gy. eur. suto 'asleep', arm. sutav 'sleep', pal. sită pret. 'slept', Ḍ. sotis 1 sg. pret.; Tor. (Biddulph) sot, f. söt 'slow'; Phal. suttu pret.; Sh. sŭtŭ 'slept, lay down'; K. sọ̆tᵘ 'calmed, extinguished', ḍoḍ. suttōrō 'asleep'; S. suto 'asleep, numb (of a limb), dead'; L. suttā pret.; WPah.jaun. sūtṇō̃ 'to sleep', (Joshi) sutṇu; Ku. sutṇo 'to lie down' (sitṇo 'to sleep' X swiṇṇo 'to dream' < *supna- ?); N. sutnu 'to sleep', B. sutā ODBL 502; Or. sutibā 'to sleep, lie flat on the ground'; Bi. Mth. sūtab 'to sleep', Bhoj. sūtal; H. sūtnā, sut° 'to sleep, lie down'; OMarw. sūto 'asleep', OG. sūtaü; Si. hot, ot 'reclining'.
    *saupta-, sauptika-.
    Addenda: suptá-: WPah.kṭg. (kc.) sútṇõ 'to sleep, fall asleep, lie down', poet. sutiṇo 'to fall asleep', caus. kc. sutarno, sətarno 'to put to sleep'; Md. ot 'placed' pp. of onnanī (absol. ove) 'lies down' < svápati.

7200.html:
7200 nidrā́ f. 'sleep' RV. [√drai]
    Pa. niddā- f. 'sleep', Pk. ṇiddā-, ṇeddā- f., Ap. ṇiṁda nom. sg. f., ṇiddaḍī- f., Gy. eur. lindr, °ra, °ri f., as. nendir, Kt. mīnɔ, Tir. nīndᵃr, Bshk. Tor. nīn f., Phal. nīdrə, nīndra, K. nĕndᵃr f., S. niṇḍra f., L. nindr f., awāṇ. nī˜dur, P. nī˜dar, nī˜d f., ḍog. nī˜dərᵊ f., Ku. nīn, N. nĩd, nin, A. nind, B. nid, nī˜d, Or. nida, Mth. nī˜d, nīn, Bhoj. niniñā, Aw.lakh. nī˜d, H. nīd, nī˜d f., OMarw. nīda f., G. nīdar, nidarṛī, nī˜d f., M. nīd f., Ko. nĩda f., Si. ninda, st. nin̆di-. — Mai. niž 'sleep' (< *niẓ with ž after i Buddruss Kan 12), Sh.gil. nir f. (→ Ḍ. ni, niya?), koh. gur. nī˜š (cf. Mai. ab.), pales. neṣ (< *neẓ, phonet. cf. yantrá- > gil. yõ̯r, koh. gur. yõṣ, stem yõẓ-). — But Mai. niž, Sh. nī˜š (if with š < final -ž), with WPah. (Joshi) nīj f. 'sleep', M. nīj̈ f. (nij̈ṇẽ 'to sleep', G. nijvũ) phonet. might be < niryā́-, niryāti or both phonet. and semant. < nípadyatē. — K. nĕh f. 'sleep' ← another Dard. dialect with *niṣ as in Sh.? — or < niśā- 'night'?? nídrāyati, nidrālú-, nidritá-.
    Addenda: nidrā́-: S.kcch. nĭ̄ndhar f. 'sleep', Garh. nind f., Md. nidi.
    dr > j: WPah.kc. nīj f. (obl. -a) 'sleep', kṭg. nīñj f., ṇīñj f. (Him.I 161 ṇ- < n- attracted by a reflex consonant group on its way from dr to jj, but poss. < *avanidrā- with unexpl. loss in MIA. of initial o/uṇi- with which the transference of an initial u- to an interior syllable may be compared, e.g. WPah. dhwāˋr < uddhāra-). On the other hand, if NIA. forms with j(j) ascribed to nidrā́- are not ← Himalayan dialects in which dr > j(j) e.g. WPah.J. jūb < *druvvā- < dūrvā-, all are poss. < niryā́-.
